items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And one of these guys has written extensively about Dave Tough, who is one of my great heroes on the drums, and I thought here’s my chance — Dave Tough, that’s what I’m going to do all night.

ctx.x: Yes. Are you sure you want to think about that? And is it usually something inherent in the rhythm section that’s not, like you said, someone’s trying to dominate or just not —

No. Because I haven’t had many train wrecks with rhythm sections. It’s been the horn players, who’ll tell you one thing and then they forgot they told you that. Or, they want to control the rhythm section. It wasn’t a train wreck, but it was a very nerve wracking experience, I played with an individual who shall remain nameless, who was feature- billed with another Swing Era musician who shall also remain nameless. And there was a slight battle of the egos before the concert and it translated into telling the…
Oh, wow. He stopped the tune and did that?
